sample_unit: nutrition questions with paired AI and RD responses

links.outcome: Reading grade level of AI and RD nutrition responses versus CDC/NIH recommendations
links.effect: Both groups averaged a 10th-grade FKGL; FRES 53.5±13.5 (RD) vs 46.2±12.5 (AI); AI used more syllables per word (1.73 vs 1.60).
links.quote: though both groups averaged a 10th-grade level on the FKGL, exceeding Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and National Institutes of Health (NIH) recommendations.

links.outcome: Readability of AI-generated nutrition responses for patients
links.effect: AI responses had lower FRES than RD responses (46.2±12.5 vs 53.5±13.5; P<0.001) and averaged a 10th-grade level, above recommended levels.
links.quote: RDs' responses were more readable, with higher FRES (53.5±13.5 vs. 46.2±12.5; P<0.001), and simpler vocabulary (1.60±0.1 vs. 1.73±0.1 syllables/word, P<0.001), though both groups averaged a 10th-grade level on the FKGL, exceeding Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and National Institutes of Health (NIH) recommendations.

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates the quality, empathy, and readability of LLM (ChatGPT-4o) responses to nutrition questions compared to human registered dietitians, but does not test a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
